warnings.text: From 2052 (age 78) your savings and investments and pension can’t cover your spending. The gap is shown as an unfunded shortfall.
You haven’t chosen what to do with your leftover money, so the projection doesn’t save any of it (it’s treated as spent).

suggestions.title: Emergency fund in place
suggestions.text: Your cash covers about 8.7 months of essential outgoings, meeting your 3-month target. Keep a small share going to it so it keeps up as your costs rise; anything beyond the target goes to your other choices.

suggestions.title: Check for employer matching
suggestions.text: Your employer adds 3%. Many employers add more if you pay more — if yours does, that’s usually the best return available.

suggestions.title: Use your ISA allowance
suggestions.text: You have about £20,000 of this year’s £20,000 ISA allowance left. Growth and interest in an ISA are tax-free. For money you won’t need for at least five years, a stocks & shares ISA has historically beaten cash, but can fall in value.
howTo: Set up £710 a month into a stocks & shares ISA (or a cash ISA for money you’ll need within five years). Open one, or top up one you already have.
You have about £20,000 of this year’s allowance left, and 163 days until it resets on 5 April 2027.
Set the payment for payday so it happens without thinking about it.

commitment.what: Pay £710 a month into an ISA
